rover_inside.rule: a rover geom held whole inside another (as MuJoCo collides it) adds no forbidden pose: an arm geom near it is nearer the other; left out (--keep-inside keeps it)

stand_ins.rule: per rover mesh: the share of its sampled surface lying more than cover_tol_m outside the parts that count as they are, the extent of that share in the rover frame (m), and the boxes standing in for it

root_link.rule: its own joints sampled every step_deg, its meshes as surface stand-ins when voxel_m is above 0 (else its geoms as they are); a contact closer than margin_m forbids every grid value within half a grid step

mount_rule: the root link touches these at every value of its joints: those contacts are not counted

fingers.rule: every finger position: each geom a finger joint moves is replaced by its swept volume (the convex hull of the geom at both ends of a slide, every 10 degrees of a hinge); the sweep's base pose holds the fingers open: each at the end of its range that spreads the gripper the most, a joint a model equality ties to another following it

upright.pushed_out_by: gripper base - original profile rails extended 22mm each end

payload.frame: the frame of the body nc90_tool (the fingers' body)
payload.rule: a cylinder held between the finger pads, swept once per orientation as an arm geom (it meets the rover parts only), the fingers at the gap that holds it: upright = its axis along the approach (where the fingers point: a can standing on the floor, picked from above), across = its axis across both the slide and the approach (a can lying down, picked from the side). Centred between the pads' inner faces and across them, its centre at the pads' middle along the approach, pushed out along the approach until it clears the hand's other geoms (pushed_out_m, pushed_out_by). The table forbids a cell when the empty gripper (every jaw position) or the payload in either orientation comes within margin_m of a rover part
payload.counts_rule: forbidden: the cells where the empty gripper, the payload held each way, and any of them (union, the table) come within margin_m of a rover part; added: those of them the empty gripper leaves free; part_counts: the cells where the payload, either way, touches that part

part_counts_rule: cells where the arm, the gripper empty, touches this part (a cell counts for every part it touches); payload.part_counts the same for the payload
pair_counts_rule: cells where this arm part and this rover part touch: the 100 most frequent pairs; pair_cells holds every pair as [i, k, cells] for arm_geoms[i] and part_names[k]
joint_map_basis: first alignment: model_zero_ticks 2048 and sign +1 on all five joints (the middle of each calibrated travel on the model's zero). Rendered on the SO-101 of the CAD scene with this map, the two poses recorded on the arm look right: drive (ticks pan 2857, lift 860, elbow 3206, flex 868, roll 3221 = pan +71.1, lift -104.4, elbow +101.8, flex -103.7, roll +103.1 deg) is the arm folded, the forearm back over the upper arm, the gripper straight up; look (ticks pan 2869, lift 1057, elbow 3208, flex 2018, roll 3220) is the forearm level, pointing ahead, the gripper forward and down (flex -2.6 deg). drive sits past the model's limits on the lift (4 deg), the elbow (5) and the wrist flex (9), look on the elbow (5): the real end stops lie past the model's (the reason for pad_deg). The pan zero is the least certain, about 15 deg either way. The final check is the operator's eyes on the robot: the same two poses, model against arm (docs/arm.md).
joint_map_rule: rad = sign * (ticks - model_zero_ticks) * 2 pi / ticks_per_rev; ticks as the servo reports them (homing offset applied); align with two poses (docs/arm.md)
occupancy_rule: occupancy: one uint8 per cell, 1 = forbidden, flat in row-major order, packed 8 cells per byte (numpy packbits, first cell in the high bit), written in hex; with a payload, occupancy_empty_bits_hex holds the empty gripper's alone, the same way
cell_part_rule: 0 = free, k = part_names[k - 1]: the rover part with the most contacts in that cell (the empty gripper's where it forbids the cell, else the payload's)
